  <!--
    Keychain access groups — the decoupling that makes a bundle-id rename survivable.

    Without this key every wallet Keychain item lands in the IMPLICIT group
    `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet`, i.e. the access group IS the
    bundle id. Renaming the bundle would make every existing item — device keys,
    Share 1, sessions, the managed-DID index — invisible, silently, with the app
    presenting as a clean install. See ADR-0030.

    ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. iOS files a new item into the FIRST entry of this array
    when the caller does not name a group, and searches EVERY entitled group when a
    read does not name one. So:

      [0] org.obsign.shared    — the stable group. Does not track the bundle id, so a
                                 rename cannot move it. New items are written here.
                                 Also the shared group MM-419's notification keys need.
      [1] dev.malpercio.…      — the legacy group, implicit until now. Listed EXPLICITLY
                                 so it stays readable after the bundle id moves, when it
                                 would otherwise stop being implicit and vanish.

    Neither entry may be removed or reordered while any install may still hold items in
    the legacy group. `just bundle-identity-check` and keychain.rs's
    `entitlement_declares_stable_group_first` test enforce both.

    Like the iCloud container, this entitlement must exist on the App ID (Apple Developer
    portal: enable Keychain Sharing with both group names, regenerate the App Store
    provisioning profile) or TestFlight signing fails with an entitlements mismatch.
  -->
  <key>keychain-access-groups</key>
  <array>
    <string>$(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared</string>
    <string>$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet</string>
  </array>
</dict>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bundle-identity-check.sh — a bundle-id rename can never land as a one-line diff.
#
# The wallet's bundle identifier is not just a string: until MM-462 it silently doubled as
# two independent addressing schemes for the user's identity material.
#
#   1. The Keychain access group. With no `keychain-access-groups` entitlement, items land in
#      the implicit `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id>` group. A rename ⇒ every item — device
#      keys, Share 1, sessions, the managed-DID index — invisible.
#   2. The iCloud container `iCloud.<bundle-id>`, which holds the repo CAR snapshot and the
#      blob mirror — MM-451's disaster-recovery source. A rename ⇒ both gone.
#
# Both fail *silently*: the app comes up looking like a clean install. A user who had not kept
# Share 3 would be unrecoverable through no action of their own.
#
# This gate pins each app's identifier and asserts the net is in place, so the rename has to be
# a deliberate edit to this file — which is where the checklist lives. See ADR-0030 and
# docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-wallet-identity-durability.md §4.
#
# Linux-runnable (greps only); part of `just ci` / `just ci-pds`.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

# --- The pins -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Changing either value is the rename. Before you do, ALL of the following must already have
# shipped and baked in a released build that users have had a full release cycle to install:
#
#   [ ] The stable Keychain access group below is declared FIRST in the app's
#       Entitlements.ios.plist, and has been in a shipped release — so items already live
#       there rather than in the implicit legacy group.
#   [ ] The legacy access group below is still declared. It stops being implicit the moment
#       the bundle id moves; only the explicit entry keeps pre-rename items readable.
#   [ ] FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER stays exactly as-is. An iCloud container id cannot be renamed;
#       Apple permits one that does not match the bundle id (ADR-0030).
#   [ ] The App ID carries Keychain Sharing (both groups) + the iCloud container, and the App
#       Store provisioning profile has been regenerated. Otherwise signing fails.
#
# A rename shipped in the same release as the access-group change strands anyone who skips
# that version. The bake time is the point.
WALLET_BUNDLE_ID='dev.malpercio.identitywallet'
ADMIN_BUNDLE_ID='dev.malpercio.admincompanion'
STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP='org.obsign.shared'
LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP='dev.malpercio.identitywallet'
FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER='iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet'

WALLET_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri"
ADMIN_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/admin-companion/src-tauri"
WALLET_ENT="${WALLET_DIR}/Entitlements.ios.plist"
WALLET_INFO="${WALLET_DIR}/Info.ios.plist"
KEYCHAIN_RS="${WALLET_DIR}/src/keychain.rs"

fail=0
note() {
  echo "bundle-identity-check: FAIL — $1" >&2
  fail=1
}

# --- 1. Identifiers match their pins -------------------------------------------------------
check_identifier() {
  local app="$1" expected="$2" conf="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/$1/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"
  local actual
  actual="$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*"identifier"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "${conf}")"
  if [ -z "${actual}" ]; then
    note "could not read the bundle identifier from ${conf}"
    return
  fi
  if [ "${actual}" != "${expected}" ]; then
    note "${app} bundle id is '${actual}' but this gate pins '${expected}'.
  A rename changes the Keychain access group AND the iCloud container at once, and both fail
  silently — the app comes up looking like a clean install. Work the checklist at the top of
  $(basename "$0"), confirm the access-group change has shipped and baked for a full release
  cycle, then update the pin in the same PR as the rename."
  fi
}
check_identifier identity-wallet "${WALLET_BUNDLE_ID}"
check_identifier admin-companion "${ADMIN_BUNDLE_ID}"

# --- 2. The access-group net ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract the keychain-access-groups <string> values in declaration order. Order is the
# mechanism: iOS writes a new item into the FIRST entitled group and searches EVERY entitled
# group on a read that names none.
groups="$(
  sed -n '/<key>keychain-access-groups<\/key>/,/<\/array>/p' "${WALLET_ENT}" |
    sed -n 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/p'
)"
if [ -z "${groups}" ]; then
  note "wallet Entitlements.ios.plist declares no keychain-access-groups — every item would
  land in the implicit \$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id> group, which a rename destroys."
else
  first="$(printf '%s\n' "${groups}" | head -n1)"
  if [ "${first}" != "\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP}" ]; then
    note "the stable group must be FIRST in keychain-access-groups (that position is what makes
  it the write target); found '${first}', expected '\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP}'."
  fi
  if ! printf '%s\n' "${groups}" | grep -qxF -- "\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP}"; then
    note "the legacy group '\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP}' is no longer declared.
  It is implicit only while the bundle id still matches it; dropping the explicit entry orphans
  every item written before the stable group existed."
  fi
fi

# The Rust constants name the same groups the entitlement declares — keychain.rs's module docs
# and its compile-time test both key off them.
for const_pair in "STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP ${STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP}" "LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP ${LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP}"; do
  name="${const_pair%% *}"
  value="${const_pair#* }"
  if ! grep -qF -- "pub const ${name}: &str = \"${value}\";" "${KEYCHAIN_RS}"; then
    note "keychain.rs's ${name} does not equal '${value}' — the entitlement and the code that
  documents it have diverged."
  fi
done

# --- 3. The iCloud container is frozen, not derived from the bundle id ----------------------
# Checked against the literal, NOT against the current bundle id: deriving it would let a
# rename silently redefine "correct" and orphan the backups this exists to protect.
if ! grep -qF -- "${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}" "${WALLET_ENT}"; then
  note "wallet Entitlements.ios.plist no longer names the frozen iCloud container
  '${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}'. A container id cannot be renamed; changing it orphans the repo
  CAR snapshot and the blob mirror (ADR-0030)."
fi
if ! grep -qF -- "${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}" "${WALLET_INFO}"; then
  note "wallet Info.ios.plist's NSUbiquitousContainers no longer names
  '${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}' — the mirror would vanish from the Files app."
fi

# --- 4. Least privilege on the console -----------------------------------------------------
# The operator console's keychain items are all re-derivable by re-pairing, so it gets no
# shared group. (ios-template-check already forbids it an iCloud container.)
if grep -qF 'keychain-access-groups' "${ADMIN_DIR}/Entitlements.ios.plist"; then
  note "admin-companion declares keychain-access-groups. Its keychain items are re-derivable by
  re-pairing, so it has no need to share a group — and sharing one would widen what the wallet's
  identity material is reachable from."
fi

if [ "${fail}" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi
echo "bundle-identity-check: OK — bundle ids pinned, access-group net declared, iCloud container frozen"

# ADR-0030: A stable Keychain access group and a frozen iCloud container, both decoupled from the bundle id

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-26
- **Deciders:** mal
- **Related:** MM-462; [MM-419](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-419) (notification keys need a shared group), [MM-451](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-451) (the iCloud backup is disaster-recovery input); `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-wallet-identity-durability.md` §4; `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/{Entitlements.ios.plist,Info.ios.plist,src/keychain.rs}`; `scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh`

## Context

The wallet ships as Obsign. Its OAuth client is `identitywallet.obsign.org`, its redirect
scheme is `org.obsign.identitywallet`, and `Info.ios.plist` already carries a legacy
`dev.malpercio.identitywallet` URL-scheme entry beside the `org.obsign` one. The iOS bundle
identifier, however, is still `dev.malpercio.identitywallet`. A rename to `org.obsign.*` is
plainly contemplated, and reads as a one-line change to `tauri.conf.json`.

It is not one line. The bundle id silently doubles as two independent addressing schemes for
everything the user's identity depends on:

1. **The Keychain access group.** With no `keychain-access-groups` entitlement, every item
   lands in the implicit `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id>` group — the access group *is*
   the bundle id. Rename it and the device keys, Share 1, the per-DID sessions, and the
   managed-DID index are all still on disk and none are reachable.
2. **The iCloud container.** `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` is hardcoded in
   `Entitlements.ios.plist` and in `Info.ios.plist`'s `NSUbiquitousContainers`. It holds the
   repo CAR snapshot and the blob mirror — the disaster-recovery source MM-451 rebuilds an
   account from, and the only backup layer that survives the PDS itself failing.

Both fail *silently*. There is no error and no degraded mode: the app comes up looking like a
clean install. A user who had not kept Share 3, and whose Share 1 lived only in the old access
group, would be unrecoverable through no action of their own.

This has not fired. The decision exists so that it cannot.

The second force is timing. Even a correct access-group change cannot be shipped in the same
release as the rename: a user who skips that version updates straight from "items in the
implicit legacy group" to "app that only knows the new group", which is the original failure
with extra steps. And an iCloud container id, unlike an access group, cannot be renamed at all —
Apple offers no migration primitive, only the option of keeping a container whose id does not
match the bundle id.

## Decision

**We will decouple both addressing schemes from the bundle id, ahead of any rename, and freeze
the iCloud container id permanently.**

1. `Entitlements.ios.plist` declares `keychain-access-groups` explicitly, in this order:
   `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared` (stable) then
   `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet` (legacy). Order is the mechanism: iOS
   files a new item into the **first** entitled group when a write names none, and searches
   **every** entitled group when a read names none. So writes land in the stable group and
   reads span stable-then-legacy without any call site naming a group.
2. No accessor in `keychain.rs` sets `kSecAttrAccessGroup`. Naming the group in Rust would
   require discovering the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix` at runtime, adding a failure mode to
   every Keychain call to re-implement a guarantee the OS already makes. The invariant that
   *is* enforced is the entitlement's shape, which no call site can observe: `keychain.rs`
   asserts it at compile time via `include_str!`, and `just bundle-identity-check` re-asserts
   it in CI.
3. The legacy group stays declared **indefinitely**. It is implicit only while the bundle id
   still matches it; the explicit entry is the sole thing keeping pre-rename items readable
   afterwards. An install that never updates never migrates, so there is no date at which
   dropping it becomes safe.
4. **The iCloud container id stays `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` forever**, including
   after the rename, and the mismatch with the bundle id is documented rather than fixed.
5. The rename may not ship until the access-group change has been in a released build for at
   least one full release cycle. `scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh` pins both apps' bundle ids
   so the rename cannot land as a one-line diff, and carries that checklist at its head.

## Consequences

- A bundle-id rename becomes survivable: keys and sessions written after this change are
  already in a group the rename does not touch, and items written before it stay readable
  through the explicit legacy entry.
- MM-419's notification keys get the shared access group they need; the plumbing lands once.
- The iCloud container id will visibly disagree with the bundle id after the rename. That is
  accepted untidiness with a documented reason — the mirrors are content-addressed and
  re-derivable from a live PDS, but the whole point of the disaster-recovery path is the case
  where no live PDS exists, so a silent loss is not worth the cosmetics.
- **The App ID must carry Keychain Sharing for both group names**, and the App Store
  provisioning profile must be regenerated, or TestFlight signing fails with an entitlements
  mismatch — the same operational step the iCloud container needed. This is a manual portal
  action that CI cannot perform or verify.
- A rename now requires a deliberate edit to the gate's pins in the same PR. That is friction
  by design; the gate's header is where the migration checklist lives.
- Entitlement order is now load-bearing in a way that reads as cosmetic. Two independent
  checks (a Rust test and a shell gate) exist because a reviewer cannot be expected to know
  that reordering an array orphans identity material.

## Alternatives considered

**Rename the bundle id and accept the loss.** Rejected outright: the loss is total, silent, and
falls on users who did nothing wrong.

**Set `kSecAttrAccessGroup` explicitly on every read and write.** This is what the issue's
definition of done literally describes, and it is more self-documenting. Rejected because the
literal group string requires the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix`, which is only discoverable at
runtime (a probe write plus an attribute read) — introducing a new failure mode into the path
that stores Share 1, in order to reproduce a default the OS already applies deterministically.
The entitlement-order mechanism achieves the same read/write behavior; the enforcement moved
into a compile-time test rather than into the hot path.

**Derive the legacy group from the current bundle id rather than pinning it.** Rejected: it
would make a rename self-consistent, silently redefining "legacy" to mean the *new* bundle id
and orphaning exactly the items the entry exists to protect.

**Ship a one-time copy from the old iCloud container to a new `iCloud.org.obsign.*` one, keeping
the old until verified.** Rejected. It is strictly more machinery than keeping the container id,
runs during a window when the app may be uninstalled or offline mid-copy, and buys only that the
container id matches the bundle id. Apple explicitly permits the mismatch.

**Rely on the entitlement alone and skip the CI gate.** Rejected: the rename still reads as a
one-line diff to a reviewer, and the entitlement's array order — the actual mechanism — is
exactly the kind of detail a tidy-up PR reorders without noticing.

  action that CI cannot perform or verify.
- A rename now requires a deliberate edit to the gate's pins in the same PR. That is friction
  by design; the gate's header is where the migration checklist lives.
- Entitlement order is now load-bearing in a way that reads as cosmetic. Two independent
  checks (a Rust test and a shell gate) exist because a reviewer cannot be expected to know
  that reordering an array orphans identity material.

## Alternatives considered

**Rename the bundle id and accept the loss.** Rejected outright: the loss is total, silent, and
falls on users who did nothing wrong.

**Set `kSecAttrAccessGroup` explicitly on every read and write.** This is what the issue's
definition of done literally describes, and it is more self-documenting. Rejected because the
literal group string requires the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix`, which is only discoverable at
runtime (a probe write plus an attribute read) — introducing a new failure mode into the path
that stores Share 1, in order to reproduce a default the OS already applies deterministically.
The entitlement-order mechanism achieves the same read/write behavior; the enforcement moved
into a compile-time test rather than into the hot path.

**Derive the legacy group from the current bundle id rather than pinning it.** Rejected: it
would make a rename self-consistent, silently redefining "legacy" to mean the *new* bundle id
and orphaning exactly the items the entry exists to protect.

**Ship a one-time copy from the old iCloud container to a new `iCloud.org.obsign.*` one, keeping
the old until verified.** Rejected. It is strictly more machinery than keeping the container id,
runs during a window when the app may be uninstalled or offline mid-copy, and buys only that the
container id matches the bundle id. Apple explicitly permits the mismatch.

**Rely on the entitlement alone and skip the CI gate.** Rejected: the rename still reads as a
one-line diff to a reviewer, and the entitlement's array order — the actual mechanism — is
exactly the kind of detail a tidy-up PR reorders without noticing.

# Architecture Decision Records

An **Architecture Decision Record (ADR)** captures a single significant
architectural decision: the context that forced it, the decision itself, and the
consequences we accepted. ADRs are the *historical record* — read them to
understand why the architecture is the way it is.

## Rules

- **ADRs are immutable once `Accepted`.** Don't rewrite history. If a decision
  changes, write a *new* ADR and mark the old one `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.
- **One decision per record.** If you're tempted to use "and", it's probably two
  ADRs.
- **Numbered sequentially**, zero-padded: `0001-...`, `0002-...`. The number is
  permanent; the slug describes the decision.
- **Status** is one of: `Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Deferred`, `Deprecated`,
  `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`. (`Deferred` = decided in principle but intentionally
  not scheduled; it waits on a named trigger.)
- Record decisions that are *already embodied in the code* too — a decision
  doesn't have to be new to be worth recording. Backfilling the load-bearing
  ones gives future readers the "why".

## Writing a new ADR

1. Copy [`adr-template.md`](adr-template.md) to
   `NNNN-short-slug.md` (next number).
2. Fill it in. Keep it tight — an ADR is a page, not a spec. Link to
   design plans / specs for detail.
3. Add it to the log below.
4. If it changes a documented fact, update the relevant doc under
   [`../`](../) in the same change.

## Log

input.new_string:
- `tauri.conf.json` bundle identifier `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` must match the iOS provisioning profile for physical device builds. It is **pinned by `just bundle-identity-check`** and cannot be renamed as a one-line diff: until MM-462 it silently doubled as the Keychain access group *and* the iCloud container id, so a rename would have made every device key, Share 1, session, and backup unreachable with no error (ADR-0030). The gate's header carries the rename checklist
- Keychain **access groups** are declared explicitly in `src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist`, and the array **order is the mechanism**: iOS files a new item into the *first* entitled group when a write names none, and searches *every* entitled group when a read names none. `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared` (`keychain::STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP`) is first, so all new items land in a group that does not track the bundle id; `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet` (`keychain::LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP`) stays declared **indefinitely** so items written before the stable group existed remain readable — it is implicit only while the bundle id still matches it, and an install that never updates never migrates. No accessor in `keychain.rs` sets `kSecAttrAccessGroup` (naming the group would require discovering the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix` at runtime, adding a failure mode to the path that stores Share 1); the entitlement's shape is asserted instead, at compile time by `keychain.rs`'s `entitlement_declares_stable_group_first` (via `include_str!`) and in CI by `just bundle-identity-check`. Adding or reordering an entry orphans live identity material — reviewers cannot be expected to know that, which is why two independent checks exist. The App ID must carry Keychain Sharing for **both** groups and the App Store provisioning profile must be regenerated, or TestFlight signing fails with an entitlements mismatch
- The iCloud container id `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` is **frozen permanently**, including after any bundle rename — a container id cannot be renamed, Apple permits one that does not match the bundle id, and losing it would silently orphan the repo CAR snapshot and blob mirror that are MM-451's disaster-recovery input. `just bundle-identity-check` asserts it against a literal, never against the current bundle id (deriving it would let a rename redefine "correct")

Until MM-462 the bundle id silently doubled as the Keychain access group *and* the iCloud container id, so a rename would have made every device key, recovery share, session, and backup unreachable with no error — see [ADR-0030](docs/architecture/decisions/0030-stable-keychain-group-and-frozen-icloud-container.md); the script's header carries the rename checklist

- `just ios-paths-check` - Verify the iOS workflows' `paths:` filters match the apps' cargo dependency graph exactly (scripts/ios-paths-check.sh; an unwatched app dependency or an entry re-widened to `crates/**` both fail — keeps pure-PDS changes from triggering the macOS lanes)

git add -A && git status --porcelain && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Decouple the wallet Keychain access group from the bundle id (MM-462)

The wallet's iOS bundle identifier silently doubled as two independent
addressing schemes for the user's identity material. With no
`keychain-access-groups` entitlement, every Keychain item landed in the
implicit `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id>` group — the access group *was*
the bundle id — and the iCloud container is `iCloud.<bundle-id>`. Renaming
`dev.malpercio.*` to `org.obsign.*`, which the OAuth client, the redirect
scheme, and a legacy URL-scheme entry all plainly contemplate, would have made
the device keys, Share 1, the per-DID sessions, the managed-DID index, the repo
CAR snapshot, and the blob mirror unreachable at once. Both fail silently: the
app comes up looking like a clean install. A user who had not kept Share 3
would be unrecoverable through no action of their own.

Declare the access group explicitly, ahead of any rename. Order is the
mechanism: iOS files a new item into the first entitled group when a write
names none and searches every entitled group when a read names none, so
`org.obsign.shared` first makes it the write target while the legacy group,
listed explicitly, stays readable after the bundle id moves — when it would
otherwise stop being implicit. No accessor names a group; resolving the literal
string would mean discovering the team's AppIdentifierPrefix at runtime, adding
a failure mode to the path that stores Share 1 to re-implement an OS guarantee.

The entitlement's shape is what no call site can observe, so it is asserted
twice: `keychain.rs` reads the tracked plist through `include_str!`, and
`just bundle-identity-check` re-asserts it alongside pinned bundle ids and the
frozen iCloud container. Reordering an array is exactly the kind of edit a
tidy-up PR makes without noticing.

The container id is frozen permanently — it cannot be renamed, Apple permits
one that does not match the bundle id, and the mirrors are MM-451's
disaster-recovery input. ADR-0030 records both decisions and the ordering
constraint: the group change must bake for a full release cycle before the
rename, or anyone who skips that version is stranded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Closes [MM-462](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-462/wallet-decouple-the-keychain-access-group-from-the-bundle-id-before).
Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-wallet-identity-durability.md` §4.

## The footgun

`Entitlements.ios.plist` declared no `keychain-access-groups`, so every wallet Keychain item landed in the **implicit** group `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet`. The access group *was* the bundle ID. The iCloud container is `iCloud.<bundle-id>` for the same reason.

The product is branded Obsign, the OAuth client is `org.obsign.identitywallet`, and `Info.ios.plist` already carries a legacy `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` URL-scheme entry beside the `org.obsign` one — the rename is clearly contemplated, and reads as a one-line diff. It is not. It would have moved **two independent addressing schemes at once**: device keys, Share 1, per-DID sessions and the managed-DID index (access group), plus the repo CAR snapshot and blob mirror (container). Both fail **silently** — the app comes up looking like a clean install. A user who hadn't kept Share 3 would be unrecoverable through no action of their own.

This has not fired. The PR makes sure it cannot.

## What landed

**1. The access group, decoupled ahead of any rename.** `keychain-access-groups` is now explicit, and the array order is the mechanism: iOS files a new item into the **first** entitled group when a write names none, and searches **every** entitled group when a read names none.

- `[0] $(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared` — stable, doesn't track the bundle ID, so a rename can't move it. New items land here. Also the shared group MM-419's notification keys need.
- `[1] $(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet` — legacy, implicit until now. Listed **explicitly** so it stays readable after the bundle ID moves, when it would otherwise stop being implicit.

So writes go stable and reads span stable-then-legacy, with no call site naming a group. That's deliberate: naming the literal string requires discovering the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix` at runtime, which means adding a failure mode to the path that stores Share 1 in order to re-implement a guarantee the OS already makes deterministically. ADR-0030 records why the DoD's literal wording was met this way.

**2. Enforcement where it's observable.** The entitlement's shape is the whole mechanism and no Rust call site can see it, so it's asserted twice — `keychain.rs` reads the tracked plist via `include_str!` (`entitlement_declares_stable_group_first`), and `just bundle-identity-check` re-asserts it in CI. Reordering an array is exactly the kind of edit a tidy-up PR makes without noticing.

**3. Container decision → [ADR-0030](docs/architecture/decisions/0030-stable-keychain-group-and-frozen-icloud-container.md).** `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` is **frozen permanently**, including after the rename. A container ID cannot be renamed; Apple permits one that doesn't match the bundle ID. The mirrors are content-addressed and re-derivable *from a live PDS* — but the whole point of MM-451's path is the case where no live PDS exists, so silently losing the disaster-recovery source isn't worth the tidiness.

**4. A gate that fails the build.** `scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh` (`just ci` / `ci-pds`) pins both apps' bundle IDs, asserts the stable group is first with the legacy one still present, asserts the container is frozen **against a literal** — never against the current bundle ID, since deriving it would let a rename silently redefine "correct" — and cross-checks the Rust constants. Its header carries the rename checklist. A rename now requires a deliberate edit to the pins in the same PR.

## The ordering constraint

**The rename must not ship in the same release as this change.** The app has to read from both groups and write to the new one for at least one full release cycle first; a user who skips that version would otherwise update straight from "items in the implicit legacy group" to "app that only knows the new group". This is documented in the ADR, in the gate's header checklist, and in both AGENTS.md files.

## Operational follow-up (manual, CI cannot verify)

Before the next TestFlight build: the App ID needs **Keychain Sharing** enabled with **both** group names, and the App Store provisioning profile regenerated. Otherwise signing fails with an entitlements mismatch — the same step the iCloud container needed.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p identity-wallet --lib keychain::` — 6 passed, including both new tests.
- RED-proved: reordering the entitlement array makes `entitlement_declares_stable_group_first` fail with the actual order in the message; the shell gate was negative-tested against both a bundle rename and a dropped legacy group.
- `shellcheck`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `ios-template-check`, `bundle-identity-check`, `changelog-check`, `docs-check` — all green.
- `cargo clippy -p identity-wallet --all-targets -- -D warnings` has 3 findings, all **pre-existing** in files this PR doesn't touch (`blob_backup.rs` ×2, the vendored swift-rs patch ×1). They survive because the wallet crate is `--exclude`d from the CI lane; filed separately rather than folded in.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

[PR #445](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/445) is open, MM-462 moved to In Review.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The issue's DoD said "keychain.rs writes stable, reads stable-then-legacy," which sounds like a code change. It isn't reachable as one: `kSecAttrAccessGroup` needs the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix`, discoverable only at runtime via a probe-write + attribute-read. Doing that would put a new failure mode in the code path that stores Share 1 — to reproduce a default iOS already applies deterministically. The entitlement's array order gets the identical read/write behavior for free.
- That trade has a cost worth naming: the mechanism becomes invisible from Rust. So the enforcement moved rather than disappeared — `include_str!` on the tracked plist makes the entitlement's shape a compile-time assertion, and the shell gate re-checks it. Reordering a plist array is precisely the edit a tidy-up PR makes without knowing it orphans device keys.
- The subtlest bug I designed around: the gate must compare the legacy group and container against **literals**, never against the current bundle ID. Deriving them would make a rename trivially self-consistent — the check would pass at the exact moment it's supposed to fire.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**What shipped, against the four DoD boxes:**
1. **Explicit entitlement** — `org.obsign.shared` first (write target), legacy `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` second (kept readable post-rename, when it stops being implicit).
2. **Ordering documented + enforced** — the bake-a-full-release-cycle constraint lives in [ADR-0030](docs/architecture/decisions/0030-stable-keychain-group-and-frozen-icloud-container.md), the gate's header checklist, and both AGENTS.md files.
3. **Container decision as ADR** — `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` frozen permanently, with the reasoning that the mirrors are only re-derivable *from a live PDS*, and MM-451's whole premise is that there isn't one.
4. **CI gate** — [scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh](scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh), wired into `just ci`/`ci-pds`, negative-tested against both a rename and a dropped legacy group.

**Two things you should know:**

- **A manual Apple portal step is now pending and CI cannot catch it.** Before the next TestFlight build, the App ID needs Keychain Sharing enabled with *both* group names and the App Store provisioning profile regenerated — same as the iCloud container needed. Without it, signing fails on an entitlements mismatch.
- I left three pre-existing clippy findings alone (`blob_backup.rs` ×2, vendored swift-rs ×1) — they're in files this PR doesn't touch, and they've accumulated because the wallet crate is `--exclude`d from the CI lane. Filed as a separate chip, including the question of whether the macOS PR-gate lane should run clippy so it can't recur.

content.text:
Good question — and it does change one leg of the argument, though not the conclusion. It also surfaced something I under-weighted in the ADR.

**What changes at n=1:** the "user who did nothing wrong is unrecoverable" framing is the weakest reason to freeze the container, and for one user it mostly evaporates. Your container is `NSUbiquitousContainerIsDocumentScopePublic: true`, so the mirror is browsable in Files.app — at n=1 a container rename is genuinely recoverable by dragging a folder. That's not true at n=100, so the ADR's stated rationale really is doing less work than I implied.

**What I under-weighted, and matters more:** a bundle ID rename isn't an update. App Store Connect treats the bundle ID as immutable for an existing app record, so `org.obsign.identitywallet` is a *new app* — a separate record, separate App ID, and on-device a separate install. That reframes both halves:

- **The iCloud container survives that cleanly.** Declare the same container ID on the new App ID and the new app sees the same iCloud Drive files, independent of what happens to the old install. Nothing about the app-identity change touches it.
- **The Keychain migration is the shakier half.** The new app reads the legacy group only while those items still exist on device. That works if you install the new app *before* deleting the old — the shared-access-group case working as designed. It relies on iOS keeping keychain items after an app is deleted otherwise, which is current behavior but something Apple has previously tried to change and reverted. I wouldn't want the device key resting on it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The team prefix in `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)` is the **Team ID**, not the bundle ID — which is why a differently-named app on the same team can declare the legacy group and read the old items at all. The whole migration hinges on that, and it's easy to misread the placeholder as bundle-scoped.
- So the two schemes fail differently under a rename: the container is *addressed* by a string you control on both App IDs, while the keychain is *stored* per-install. Same-looking problem, different durability.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**My recommendation: keep the freeze, but rewrite why.** Keeping the container costs nothing — no migration step, no window where the app is mid-copy, one less thing to get right during a change that's already creating a new app record. The cosmetic win is invisible anyway; the container ID never surfaces to you, and the Files.app folder already reads "Obsign" via `NSUbiquitousContainerName`.

Two things worth your call:

1. **Is n=1 a durable assumption?** The whole product premise is other people holding sovereign identities. If that changes before the rename ships, the keychain ordering constraint has to be honored for real — and by then a container migration would be back to being a bad idea. Freezing now keeps the option open in the direction that's hard to reverse.
2. **The rename plan needs the "it's a new app" fact in it.** That's more consequential than the container question and isn't written down anywhere yet — install-new-before-deleting-old is a sequencing requirement, not a detail.

Want me to amend ADR-0030 on the open PR? I'd replace the user-harm rationale with the app-identity one, and add the new-app-record constraint to the rename checklist in the gate header. Small diff, and it's the reasoning a future reader would actually need.

# ADR-0030: A stable Keychain access group and a frozen iCloud container, both decoupled from the bundle id

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-26
- **Deciders:** mal
- **Related:** MM-462; [MM-419](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-419) (notification keys need a shared group), [MM-451](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-451) (the iCloud backup is disaster-recovery input); `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-wallet-identity-durability.md` §4; `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/{Entitlements.ios.plist,Info.ios.plist,src/keychain.rs}`; `scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh`

## Context

The wallet ships as Obsign. Its OAuth client is `identitywallet.obsign.org`, its redirect
scheme is `org.obsign.identitywallet`, and `Info.ios.plist` already carries a legacy
`dev.malpercio.identitywallet` URL-scheme entry beside the `org.obsign` one. The iOS bundle
identifier, however, is still `dev.malpercio.identitywallet`. A rename to `org.obsign.*` is
plainly contemplated, and reads as a one-line change to `tauri.conf.json`.

It is not one line. The bundle id silently doubles as two independent addressing schemes for
everything the user's identity depends on:

1. **The Keychain access group.** With no `keychain-access-groups` entitlement, every item
   lands in the implicit `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id>` group — the access group *is*
   the bundle id. Rename it and the device keys, Share 1, the per-DID sessions, and the
   managed-DID index are all still on disk and none are reachable.
2. **The iCloud container.** `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` is hardcoded in
   `Entitlements.ios.plist` and in `Info.ios.plist`'s `NSUbiquitousContainers`. It holds the
   repo CAR snapshot and the blob mirror — the disaster-recovery source MM-451 rebuilds an
   account from, and the only backup layer that survives the PDS itself failing.

Both fail *silently*. There is no error and no degraded mode: the app comes up looking like a
clean install. A user who had not kept Share 3, and whose Share 1 lived only in the old access
group, would be unrecoverable through no action of their own.

This has not fired. The decision exists so that it cannot.

The second force is timing. Even a correct access-group change cannot be shipped in the same
release as the rename: a user who skips that version updates straight from "items in the
implicit legacy group" to "app that only knows the new group", which is the original failure
with extra steps. And an iCloud container id, unlike an access group, cannot be renamed at all —
Apple offers no migration primitive, only the option of keeping a container whose id does not
match the bundle id.

## Decision

**We will decouple both addressing schemes from the bundle id, ahead of any rename, and freeze
the iCloud container id permanently.**

1. `Entitlements.ios.plist` declares `keychain-access-groups` explicitly, in this order:
   `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared` (stable) then
   `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet` (legacy). Order is the mechanism: iOS
   files a new item into the **first** entitled group when a write names none, and searches
   **every** entitled group when a read names none. So writes land in the stable group and
   reads span stable-then-legacy without any call site naming a group.
2. No accessor in `keychain.rs` sets `kSecAttrAccessGroup`. Naming the group in Rust would
   require discovering the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix` at runtime, adding a failure mode to
   every Keychain call to re-implement a guarantee the OS already makes. The invariant that
   *is* enforced is the entitlement's shape, which no call site can observe: `keychain.rs`
   asserts it at compile time via `include_str!`, and `just bundle-identity-check` re-asserts
   it in CI.
3. The legacy group stays declared **indefinitely**. It is implicit only while the bundle id
   still matches it; the explicit entry is the sole thing keeping pre-rename items readable
   afterwards. An install that never updates never migrates, so there is no date at which
   dropping it becomes safe.
4. **The iCloud container id stays `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` forever**, including
   after the rename, and the mismatch with the bundle id is documented rather than fixed.
5. The rename may not ship until the access-group change has been in a released build for at
   least one full release cycle. `scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh` pins both apps' bundle ids
   so the rename cannot land as a one-line diff, and carries that checklist at its head.

## Consequences

- A bundle-id rename becomes survivable: keys and sessions written after this change are
  already in a group the rename does not touch, and items written before it stay readable
  through the explicit legacy entry.
- MM-419's notification keys get the shared access group they need; the plumbing lands once.
- The iCloud container id will visibly disagree with the bundle id after the rename. That is
  accepted untidiness with a documented reason — the mirrors are content-addressed and

# ADR-0030: A stable Keychain access group and a frozen iCloud container, both decoupled from the bundle id

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-26
- **Deciders:** mal
- **Related:** MM-462; [MM-419](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-419) (notification keys need a shared group), [MM-451](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-451) (the iCloud backup is disaster-recovery input); `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-wallet-identity-durability.md` §4; `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/{Entitlements.ios.plist,Info.ios.plist,src/keychain.rs}`; `scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh`

## Context

The wallet ships as Obsign. Its OAuth client is `identitywallet.obsign.org`, its redirect
scheme is `org.obsign.identitywallet`, and `Info.ios.plist` already carries a legacy
`dev.malpercio.identitywallet` URL-scheme entry beside the `org.obsign` one. The iOS bundle
identifier, however, is still `dev.malpercio.identitywallet`. A rename to `org.obsign.*` is
plainly contemplated, and reads as a one-line change to `tauri.conf.json`.

It is not one line. The bundle id silently doubles as two independent addressing schemes for
everything the user's identity depends on:

1. **The Keychain access group.** With no `keychain-access-groups` entitlement, every item
   lands in the implicit `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id>` group — the access group *is*
   the bundle id. Rename it and the device keys, Share 1, the per-DID sessions, and the
   managed-DID index are all still on disk and none are reachable.
2. **The iCloud container.** `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` is hardcoded in
   `Entitlements.ios.plist` and in `Info.ios.plist`'s `NSUbiquitousContainers`. It holds the
   repo CAR snapshot and the blob mirror — the disaster-recovery source MM-451 rebuilds an
   account from, and the only backup layer that survives the PDS itself failing.

Both fail *silently*. There is no error and no degraded mode: the app comes up looking like a
clean install. A user who had not kept Share 3, and whose Share 1 lived only in the old access
group, would be unrecoverable through no action of their own.

This has not fired. The decision exists so that it cannot.

The second force is that **a bundle-id rename is not an update — it is a new app.** App Store
Connect treats the bundle id as immutable for an existing app record, so `org.obsign.*` means a
new record, a new App ID, and on-device a separate install rather than an upgrade in place.
That reframes both addressing schemes, and it does so asymmetrically:

- The **iCloud container** is addressed by a string we can declare on *both* App IDs. The same
  container id on the new App ID resolves to the same iCloud Drive files, wholly independent of
  what happens to the old install. It survives the app-identity change cleanly.
- The **Keychain** is stored per-install. `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)` expands to the *Team* id, not
  the bundle id, which is what lets a differently-named app on the same team read the old
  items at all — but only while those items still exist on the device. That holds if the new
  app is installed *before* the old one is deleted (the shared-access-group case working as
  designed). Otherwise it rests on iOS retaining Keychain items after an app is deleted, which
  is current behavior but something Apple has previously shipped a change to and reverted. That
  is not a footing for the device key.

The third force is timing, and it is now dated. Even a correct access-group change cannot ship
in the same release as the rename: a user who skips that version goes straight from "items in
the implicit legacy group" to "app that only knows the new group", which is the original
failure with extra steps. A **public TestFlight is imminent**, so the population that can be
stranded stops being hypothetical shortly. An iCloud container id, unlike an access group,
cannot be renamed at all — Apple offers no migration primitive, only the option of keeping a
container whose id does not match the bundle id.

Note what is *not* load-bearing here. An earlier reading justified the freeze mainly by user
harm — a user losing their backups through no action of their own. With a single user that
argument nearly evaporates: the container is `NSUbiquitousContainerIsDocumentScopePublic`, so
one person can migrate it by dragging a folder in Files.app. The decision does not rest on
that, and should not, because the property that makes it right is structural rather than
demographic.

## Decision

**We will decouple both addressing schemes from the bundle id, ahead of any rename, and freeze
the iCloud container id permanently.**

1. `Entitlements.ios.plist` declares `keychain-access-groups` explicitly, in this order:
   `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared` (stable) then
   `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet` (legacy). Order is the mechanism: iOS
   files a new item into the **first** entitled group when a write names none, and searches
   **every** entitled group when a read names none. So writes land in the stable group and
   reads span stable-then-legacy without any call site naming a group.
2. No accessor in `keychain.rs` sets `kSecAttrAccessGroup`. Naming the group in Rust would
   require discovering the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix` at runtime, adding a failure mode to
   every Keychain call to re-implement a guarantee the OS already makes. The invariant that
   *is* enforced is the entitlement's shape, which no call site can observe: `keychain.rs`
   asserts it at compile time via `include_str!`, and `just bundle-identity-check` re-asserts
   it in CI.
3. The legacy group stays declared **indefinitely**. It is implicit only while the bundle id
   still matches it; the explicit entry is the sole thing keeping pre-rename items readable
   afterwards. An install that never updates never migrates, so there is no date at which
   dropping it becomes safe.
4. **The iCloud container id stays `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` forever**, including
   after the rename, and the mismatch with the bundle id is documented rather than fixed.
5. The rename may not ship until the access-group change has been in a released build for at
   least one full release cycle. `scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh` pins both apps' bundle ids
   so the rename cannot land as a one-line diff, and carries that checklist at its head.

- A rename now requires a deliberate edit to the gate's pins in the same PR. That is friction

- Entitlement order is now load-bearing in a way that reads as cosmetic. Two independent
  checks (a Rust test and a shell gate) exist because a reviewer cannot be expected to know

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bundle-identity-check.sh — a bundle-id rename can never land as a one-line diff.
#
# The wallet's bundle identifier is not just a string: until MM-462 it silently doubled as
# two independent addressing schemes for the user's identity material.
#
#   1. The Keychain access group. With no `keychain-access-groups` entitlement, items land in
#      the implicit `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id>` group. A rename ⇒ every item — device
#      keys, Share 1, sessions, the managed-DID index — invisible.
#   2. The iCloud container `iCloud.<bundle-id>`, which holds the repo CAR snapshot and the
#      blob mirror — MM-451's disaster-recovery source. A rename ⇒ both gone.
#
# Both fail *silently*: the app comes up looking like a clean install. A user who had not kept
# Share 3 would be unrecoverable through no action of their own.
#
# This gate pins each app's identifier and asserts the net is in place, so the rename has to be
# a deliberate edit to this file — which is where the checklist lives. See ADR-0030 and
# docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-wallet-identity-durability.md §4.
#
# Linux-runnable (greps only); part of `just ci` / `just ci-pds`.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

# --- The pins -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Changing either value is the rename. Before you do, ALL of the following must already have
# shipped and baked in a released build that users have had a full release cycle to install:
#
#   [ ] The stable Keychain access group below is declared FIRST in the app's
#       Entitlements.ios.plist, and has been in a shipped release — so items already live
#       there rather than in the implicit legacy group.
#   [ ] The legacy access group below is still declared. It stops being implicit the moment
#       the bundle id moves; only the explicit entry keeps pre-rename items readable.
#   [ ] FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER stays exactly as-is. An iCloud container id cannot be renamed;
#       Apple permits one that does not match the bundle id (ADR-0030).
#   [ ] The App ID carries Keychain Sharing (both groups) + the iCloud container, and the App
#       Store provisioning profile has been regenerated. Otherwise signing fails.
#
# A rename shipped in the same release as the access-group change strands anyone who skips
# that version. The bake time is the point.
WALLET_BUNDLE_ID='dev.malpercio.identitywallet'
ADMIN_BUNDLE_ID='dev.malpercio.admincompanion'
STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP='org.obsign.shared'
LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP='dev.malpercio.identitywallet'
FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER='iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet'

WALLET_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri"
ADMIN_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/admin-companion/src-tauri"
WALLET_ENT="${WALLET_DIR}/Entitlements.ios.plist"
WALLET_INFO="${WALLET_DIR}/Info.ios.plist"
KEYCHAIN_RS="${WALLET_DIR}/src/keychain.rs"

fail=0
note() {
  echo "bundle-identity-check: FAIL — $1" >&2
  fail=1
}

# --- 1. Identifiers match their pins -------------------------------------------------------
check_identifier() {
  local app="$1" expected="$2" conf="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/$1/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"
  local actual
  actual="$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*"identifier"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "${conf}")"
  if [ -z "${actual}" ]; then
    note "could not read the bundle identifier from ${conf}"
    return
  fi
  if [ "${actual}" != "${expected}" ]; then
    note "${app} bundle id is '${actual}' but this gate pins '${expected}'.
  A rename changes the Keychain access group AND the iCloud container at once, and both fail
  silently — the app comes up looking like a clean install. Work the checklist at the top of
  $(basename "$0"), confirm the access-group change has shipped and baked for a full release
  cycle, then update the pin in the same PR as the rename."
  fi
}
check_identifier identity-wallet "${WALLET_BUNDLE_ID}"
check_identifier admin-companion "${ADMIN_BUNDLE_ID}"

# --- 2. The access-group net ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract the keychain-access-groups <string> values in declaration order. Order is the
# mechanism: iOS writes a new item into the FIRST entitled group and searches EVERY entitled
# group on a read that names none.
groups="$(
  sed -n '/<key>keychain-access-groups<\/key>/,/<\/array>/p' "${WALLET_ENT}" |
    sed -n 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/p'
)"
if [ -z "${groups}" ]; then
  note "wallet Entitlements.ios.plist declares no keychain-access-groups — every item would
  land in the implicit \$(AppIdentifierPrefix)<bundle-id> group, which a rename destroys."
else
  first="$(printf '%s\n' "${groups}" | head -n1)"
  if [ "${first}" != "\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP}" ]; then
    note "the stable group must be FIRST in keychain-access-groups (that position is what makes
  it the write target); found '${first}', expected '\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP}'."
  fi
  if ! printf '%s\n' "${groups}" | grep -qxF -- "\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP}"; then
    note "the legacy group '\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)${LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP}' is no longer declared.
  It is implicit only while the bundle id still matches it; dropping the explicit entry orphans
  every item written before the stable group existed."
  fi
fi

# The Rust constants name the same groups the entitlement declares — keychain.rs's module docs
# and its compile-time test both key off them.
for const_pair in "STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP ${STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP}" "LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP ${LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP}"; do
  name="${const_pair%% *}"
  value="${const_pair#* }"
  if ! grep -qF -- "pub const ${name}: &str = \"${value}\";" "${KEYCHAIN_RS}"; then
    note "keychain.rs's ${name} does not equal '${value}' — the entitlement and the code that
  documents it have diverged."
  fi
done

# --- 3. The iCloud container is frozen, not derived from the bundle id ----------------------
# Checked against the literal, NOT against the current bundle id: deriving it would let a
# rename silently redefine "correct" and orphan the backups this exists to protect.
if ! grep -qF -- "${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}" "${WALLET_ENT}"; then
  note "wallet Entitlements.ios.plist no longer names the frozen iCloud container
  '${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}'. A container id cannot be renamed; changing it orphans the repo
  CAR snapshot and the blob mirror (ADR-0030)."
fi
if ! grep -qF -- "${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}" "${WALLET_INFO}"; then
  note "wallet Info.ios.plist's NSUbiquitousContainers no longer names
  '${FROZEN_ICLOUD_CONTAINER}' — the mirror would vanish from the Files app."
fi

# --- 4. Least privilege on the console -----------------------------------------------------
# The operator console's keychain items are all re-derivable by re-pairing, so it gets no
# shared group. (ios-template-check already forbids it an iCloud container.)
if grep -qF 'keychain-access-groups' "${ADMIN_DIR}/Entitlements.ios.plist"; then
  note "admin-companion declares keychain-access-groups. Its keychain items are re-derivable by
  re-pairing, so it has no need to share a group — and sharing one would widen what the wallet's
  identity material is reachable from."
fi

if [ "${fail}" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi
echo "bundle-identity-check: OK — bundle ids pinned, access-group net declared, iCloud container frozen"

- The `src/lib/ipc/` modules are the only files that call `invoke()` directly (each domain module — account, oauth, appearance, claim, identity, monitor, recovery, migration, handle-change, agents, app-passwords — re-exported from `src/lib/ipc/index.ts`); page components import from `$lib/ipc`. `authenticateBiometric` is a policy gate, not an `invoke()` wrapper, and lives in `$lib/biometric.ts` (matching the sibling admin-companion app's layout)

-- `tauri.conf.json` bundle identifier `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` must match the iOS provisioning profile for physical device builds. It is **pinned by `just bundle-identity-check`** and cannot be renamed as a one-line diff: until MM-462 it silently doubled as the Keychain access group *and* the iCloud container id, so a rename would have made every device key, Share 1, session, and backup unreachable with no error (ADR-0030). The gate's header carries the rename checklist

+- `tauri.conf.json` bundle identifier `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` must match the iOS provisioning profile for physical device builds. It is **pinned by `just bundle-identity-check`** and cannot be renamed as a one-line diff: until MM-462 it silently doubled as the Keychain access group *and* the iCloud container id, so a rename would have made every device key, Share 1, session, and backup unreachable with no error (ADR-0030). A rename is also **not an update** — App Store Connect treats the bundle id as immutable for an existing app record, so `org.obsign.*` means a new record, a new App ID, and a separate on-device install; users must install the new app *before* deleting the old, and nothing may depend on Keychain items outliving deletion of the old install. The gate's header carries the full rename checklist

- Keychain **access groups** are declared explicitly in `src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist`, and the array **order is the mechanism**: iOS files a new item into the *first* entitled group when a write names none, and searches *every* entitled group when a read names none. `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared` (`keychain::STABLE_ACCESS_GROUP`) is first, so all new items land in a group that does not track the bundle id; `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)dev.malpercio.identitywallet` (`keychain::LEGACY_ACCESS_GROUP`) stays declared **indefinitely** so items written before the stable group existed remain readable — it is implicit only while the bundle id still matches it, and an install that never updates never migrates. No accessor in `keychain.rs` sets `kSecAttrAccessGroup` (naming the group would require discovering the team's `AppIdentifierPrefix` at runtime, adding a failure mode to the path that stores Share 1); the entitlement's shape is asserted instead, at compile time by `keychain.rs`'s `entitlement_declares_stable_group_first` (via `include_str!`) and in CI by `just bundle-identity-check`. Adding or reordering an entry orphans live identity material — reviewers cannot be expected to know that, which is why two independent checks exist. The App ID must carry Keychain Sharing for **both** groups and the App Store provisioning profile must be regenerated, or TestFlight signing fails with an entitlements mismatch

- The iCloud container id `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` is **frozen permanently**, including after any bundle rename — a container id cannot be renamed, Apple permits one that does not match the bundle id, and losing it would silently orphan the repo CAR snapshot and blob mirror that are MM-451's disaster-recovery input. `just bundle-identity-check` asserts it against a literal, never against the current bundle id (deriving it would let a rename redefine "correct")
- `src-tauri/gen/` is never committed -- regenerate with `cargo tauri ios init`

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Amend ADR-0030: the rename is a new app record, not an update

Review question — "I'm the only user, does that change the container
calculus?" — exposed that the ADR's stated rationale was the weakest leg of the
argument. At one user, "loses their backups through no action of their own"
nearly evaporates: the container is document-scope public, so one person can
migrate it by hand in Files.app. The decision should not rest on a demographic
fact, and a public TestFlight is imminent, so it will not stay true.

The structural reason is better and was under-weighted. App Store Connect
treats the bundle id as immutable for an existing app record, so org.obsign.*
is a new record, a new App ID, and a separate on-device install rather than an
upgrade. That splits the two schemes: the container is addressed by a string
declarable on both App IDs and survives cleanly, while the Keychain is stored
per-install and survives only if the new app is installed before the old is
deleted — otherwise resting on iOS retaining items after deletion, which Apple
has shipped a change to and reverted. Not a footing for the device key.

Record the sequencing obligation where it will be read (the gate's checklist
and the wallet AGENTS.md, not only the ADR), since the app cannot enforce it.
Add the timing point that follows: shipping this before the first public
TestFlight means a tester never has a legacy-group-only install, which is the
difference between a rename that must migrate a population and one that only
tolerates a shrinking tail. That window closes when TestFlight opens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push 2>&1 | tail -2
